description: Reference parts for a single-cylinder four-stroke engine, from the standard textbook description of the Otto cycle: 'The piston, sealed by rings in the cylinder, is driven by combustion pressure through the connecting rod to the crankshaft; valves in the cylinder head, timed by the camshaft, let the mixture in and the exhaust out; the flywheel carries the crankshaft between power strokes.'
sources: J. B. Heywood, Internal Combustion Engine Fundamentals, McGraw-Hill (1988), ch. 1.2 'Engine components' — canonical spark-ignition component list
Wikipedia, 'Four-stroke engine' and 'Piston engine' component figures (retrieved 2026-10-14)
notes: 17 lowercase names. Gate 3 requires recall >= 0.8 (>= 14 of 17) among the figure's [data-part] names, casefolded. Matching is exact on the casefolded trimmed string; synonyms are not credited — the figure must use the textbook name.
